cards.title: Hepatic vs. Renal Elimination in Small-Molecule Scaling
cards.claim: Elimination pathway helps qualify small-molecule clearance scaling. In the cited multi-compound evaluation, simple allometry performed better on average for predominantly renal elimination than for hepatic elimination, particularly low-extraction hepatic compounds. Maximum life-span potential (MLP) or brain-weight (BRW) corrections were empirical alternatives, not guaranteed improvements for a new compound.
conditions: A small molecule is being evaluated for cross-species clearance scaling.
The renal/hepatic contribution and relevant binding or extraction context are supported.
Candidate correction methods are explicitly defined and compared rather than triggered as universal physiological rules.
required_inputs: Animal clearance with species, route, blood/plasma and total/unbound basis, units, body weight and uncertainty.
Target-species body weight for the intended projection.
Supported renal/hepatic contribution and binding/extraction context.
Maximum life-span potential (MLP) values only if evaluating an MLP-corrected candidate.
Brain weight (BRW) values only if evaluating a BRW-corrected candidate.
Simple-allometry exponent and its uncertainty when estimated from the animal data; this is a downstream estimate, not a raw measurement.
limitations: Average method performance in the reference dataset is not target-specific accuracy.
Low extraction and species-specific metabolism can leave substantial uncertainty.
No fixed exponent boundary alone establishes that MLP or BRW correction is appropriate.
cards.downstream_use: Use elimination-pathway evidence to compare scaling candidates and retain method uncertainty.

note: Method/reference scope retained; source identity is available in original evidence.
